That matters because any real push from Ewers keeps Miami’s QB role unsettled, which can affect pass-game continuity and weekly fantasy stability. [2, 4]

- **Ollie Gordon II (RB)** — Gordon is being framed as Miami’s running back wild card, with the door open for him to climb if he looks like the productive runner he was in college. For fantasy, that’s a touch-count watch: he’s the kind of back who could force his way into the rotation if the depth chart stays fluid. [2]

- **Mike McDaniel (HC)** — McDaniel’s Miami offenses have consistently generated strong yards-after-catch output per reception over the last three seasons, signaling a scheme that wants pass-catchers working in space. That’s a useful fantasy lens for the Dolphins’ receivers and tight ends, especially if the offense leans into manufactured touches and YAC chances again. [5]
